column5: description
Aragorn (Sindarin: [ˈaraɡɔrn]) is a fictional character and a protagonist in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.
Arwen Undómiel is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.
Balin is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's world of Middle-earth.
Bard the Bowman is a character in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit.
Beorn is a character created by J. R. R. Tolkien as part of his Middle-earth legendarium.

Bilbo Baggins (Westron: Bilba Labingi) is the title character and protagonist of J. R. R. Tolkien's 1937 novel The Hobbit, a supporting character in The Lord of the Rings, and the fictional narrator (along with Frodo Baggins) of many of Tolkien's Middle-earth writings.
Boromir is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Celebrimbor (Sindarin pronunciation: [ˌkɛlɛˈbrimbɔr]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Denethor II, son of Ecthelion II, is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's novel The Lord of the Rings.

In J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth writings, the Dúnedain (Sindarin pronunciation: [ˈduːnɛˌdaɪn]; sing. Dúnadan; lit. 'Man of the West') were a race of Men, also known as the Númenóreans or Men of Westernesse (translated from the Sindarin term).
Elendil (Quenya: [ɛˈlendil]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Elrond Half-elven is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.
In J. R. R. Tolkien's writings, Elves are the first fictional race to appear in Middle-earth.
Eärendil (Quenya pronunciation: [ɛ.aˈrɛn.dil]) the Mariner and his wife Elwing are characters in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.
Faramir  is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.
Fingolfin (Sindarin: [fiŋˈɡolfin]) is a character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium, appearing in The Silmarillion.
Finwë (Quenya: [ˈfinwɛ]) and  Míriel  (Quenya: [ˈmiːriɛl]) are fictional characters from J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Frodo Baggins is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's writings and one of the protagonists in The Lord of the Rings.
Fëanor (Quenya pronunciation: [ˈfɛ.anɔr]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Silmarillion.
Galadriel (IPA: [ɡaˈladri.ɛl]) is a character created by J. R. R. Tolkien in his Middle-earth writings.
Gandalf, in longer form Gandalf the Grey and later Gandalf the White, is a protagonist in J. R. R. Tolkien's novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.
Gil-galad is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium, the last High King of the Noldor, one of the main divisions of Elves.
Gimli is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth, appearing in The Lord of the Rings.
Glorfindel (Sindarin pronunciation: [ɡlɔrˈfindɛl]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.
Goldberry is a character from the works of the author J. R. R. Tolkien.
Gollum is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy world of Middle-earth.
Gríma, called (the) Wormtongue, is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.
Húrin is a fictional character in the Middle-earth legendarium of J. R. R. Tolkien.
Isildur (Quenya: [iˈsildur]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth, the elder son of Elendil, descended from Elros, the founder of the island Kingdom of Númenor.
Legolas (Sindarin: [ˈlɛɡɔlas]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.
Lúthien and Beren are characters in J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy world Middle-earth.
Melian is a fictional character in J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.

Meriadoc Brandybuck (Westron: Kalimac Brandagamba; usually called Merry) is a Hobbit, a fictional character from J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium, featured throughout his most famous work, The Lord of the Rings.

The fictional races and peoples that appear in J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy world of Middle-earth include the seven listed in Appendix F of The Lord of the Rings: Elves, Men, Dwarves, Hobbits, Ents, Orcs and Trolls, as well as spirits such as the Valar and Maiar.

Morgoth Bauglir ([ˈmɔrɡɔθ ˈbau̯ɡlir]; originally Melkor [ˈmɛlkor]) is the primary antagonist of Tolkien's legendarium, the mythic epic by the English author J. R. R. Tolkien and published in parts as The Silmarillion, The Children of Húrin, Beren and Lúthien, and The Fall of Gondolin.

In the works of J. R. R. Tolkien, the Noldor (also spelled Ñoldor, meaning those with knowledge in his constructed language Quenya) are a kindred of Elves who migrate west to the blessed realm of Valinor from the continent of Middle-earth, splitting from other groups of Elves as they went.
Peregrin Took (Westron: Razanur Tûk), commonly known simply as Pippin, is a fictional character from J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy novel The Lord of the Rings.
Radagast the Brown is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Samwise Gamgee (, usually called Sam) (Westron: Banazîr Galbasi) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth.
Saruman, also called Saruman the White, later Saruman of Many Colours, is a fictional character and an antagonist in J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy novel The Lord of the Rings.
Sauron () is the title character and the main antagonist of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, where he rules the land of Mordor.
Shelob is a fictional monster in the form of a giant spider from J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.
Smaug () is a dragon and the main antagonist in J. R. R. Tolkien's 1937 novel The Hobbit, his treasure and the mountain he lives in being the goal of the quest.
Elu Thingol or Elwë Singollo is a fictional character in J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.
Thorin Oakenshield (Thorin II) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's 1937 novel The Hobbit.
Thranduil is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.
Théoden is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy novel, The Lord of the Rings.
Tom Bombadil is a character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Treebeard, or Fangorn in Sindarin, is a tree-giant character in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.
Tuor Eladar and Idril Celebrindal are fictional characters from J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth legendarium.
Túrin Turambar (pronounced [ˈtuːrɪn tuˈrambar]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Ungoliant (Sindarin pronunciation: [ʊŋˈɡɔljant]) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium, described as an evil spirit in the form of a giant spider.
The Watcher in the Water is a fictional creature in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth; it appears in The Fellowship of the Ring, the first volume of The Lord of the Rings.
The Lord of the Nazgûl, also called the Witch-king of Angmar, the Pale King, or Black Captain, is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy novel The Lord of the Rings.

column2: Women in The Lord of the Rings
column5: The roles of women in The Lord of the Rings have often been assessed as insignificant, or important only in relation to male characters in a story about men for boys.
Éomer is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth.
Éowyn ( or ) is a fictional character in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.
